n engl j med 377;4 nejm.org July 27, 2017 357 Abiraterone plus Prednisone in Prostate Cancer We explored the utility of more effective blockade of the androgen-receptor axis with the addition of abiraterone to androgen-deprivation therapy in men with metastatic, castration-sensi- tive prostate cancer. Our data support the hypoth- esis that more effective inhibition of androgen- receptor signaling as a component of the initial systemic therapy in patients with castration- sensitive prostate cancer leads to improved out- comes. The clinical benefit that we observed con- trasts with that from the many previous attempts with castration and first-generation androgen- receptor inhibitors,27,28 which showed only a small improvement with a combined androgen- blockade approach,29 presumably owing to the lower potency and partial agonist activity of these drugs. Several other ongoing randomized, phase 3 trials in this patient population are ex- amining androgen receptor-signaling combina- tion therapies with androgen-deprivation ther apy (Table S7 in the Supplementary Appendix) and are exploring whether these treatments can be added to androgen-deprivation therapy plus docetaxel in patients with metastatic, castration- sensitive prostate cancer. The assessment of effi- cacy of subsequent therapies, including the types of disease progression in patients who were re- ceiving treatment, will require more long-term analysis. Men with newly diagnosed, metastatic, castra- tion-sensitive prostate cancer can have variable outcomes, so we purposely enrolled those who were considered to have at least two high-risk prognostic features (e.g., a Gleason score of ≥8, the presence of ≥3 bone lesions, or the presence of measurable visceral metastasis),30-33 all of which are associated with poor survival. In addition, 50% of the patients had symptomatic disease at baseline. The patient population appears to be similar to high-burden disease populations in the three randomized trials that evaluated andro- gen-deprivation therapy plus docetaxel,3,5,7 since the outcomes in the control groups were similar across those studies. After a median follow-up of 7 years in GETUG-15, a nonsignificant 22% reduction in the relative risk of death was ob- served in patients with high-volume disease.8 A significant 27% reduction in the relative risk of death (and a reduction of 37% in patients with high-volume disease) with androgen-deprivation therapy plus docetaxel was observed after a 53.7- month follow-up (approximately 50% of deaths) in CHAARTED.6 In STAMPEDE, a significant 24% risk reduction in death was observed among pa- tients with metastatic, castration-sensitive pros- tate cancer.7 (The STAMPEDE investigators now report in the Journal the results of another trial of abiraterone plus prednisone in men with local ly advanced or metastatic prostate cancer.34) In our trial, the efficacy of abiraterone, with a 38% reduction in the risk of death among patients who had not received previous treatment for metastatic disease, compares favorably with pre- vious findings. results.relation_rationale: The abstract reports higher rates of grade 3 hypertension and hypokalemia. The closest complete comparative table result is grade 3 hypertension, a specified severity subset of the broader adverse-events outcome, with arm-specific counts and percentages reported for both randomized groups. Hypokalemia is reported separately in the same table and is not silently combined with hypertension because the source does not define a composite endpoint.

applicability.rationale: The main report describes a phase 3 randomized 1:1 trial assigning patients to abiraterone plus prednisone plus ADT or dual placebo plus ADT.

measurement.method: Grade 3 hypertension, assessed and graded using the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 4.0.

time_point_or_window.description: Treatment-emergent assessment from Study Day 1 through 30 days after the last dose of study drug

comparison_groups.assignment: Abiraterone acetate 1000 mg daily plus prednisone 5 mg daily with androgen-deprivation therapy
Matched abiraterone and prednisone placebos with androgen-deprivation therapy

reported.analysis_population: Safety population: patients in the two randomized groups who received study drug; the table denominators are N=597 in the abiraterone group and N=602 in the placebo group.

assessments.scope_justification: The selected table passage reports hypertension by severity, including grade 3, with complete arm headers, denominators, and values: 121 (20%) versus 59 (10%). The protocol/SAP specifies CTCAE version 4.0 grading and treatment-emergent collection from Study Day 1 through 30 days after last dose.
assessments.population_justification: The table is reported for the abiraterone and placebo safety groups (N=597 and N=602). The protocol defines the safety population as subjects receiving at least one dose, distinct from the ITT population; no all-randomized denominator is substituted.
unknowns: The table does not provide participant-level missingness accounting for hypertension ascertainment beyond the reported safety-group denominators.
The source reports hypokalemia as a separate adverse-event row, so no composite hypertension/hypokalemia estimate is inferred.
